record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let (K,v) be a henselian valued field. Assume that every algebraic extension of (K,v) is an independent defect field in the sense defined in the paper via Galois extensions of prime degree with nontrivial defect. Does it follow that (K,v) must already be a roughly deeply ramified field?

evidence.quote:
In view of Theorem 9, we conjecture that a henselian field is a roughly deeply
ramified field if and only if all of its algebraic extensions are independent defect
fields. Thus we ask:

Open problem 16: If all algebraic extensions of a henselian field (K, v) are
independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified
field?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(K,v)$ be a henselian valued field, with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_v$, value group $vK$, and residue field $Kv$. For a finite extension $(L|K,v)$, write $e(L|K) = (vL : vK)$ for the ramification index, $f(L|K) = [Lv : Kv]$ for the residue degree, and define the defect $d(L|K)$ by the fundamental equality
$$[L:K] \;=\; d(L|K)\cdot e(L|K)\cdot f(L|K),$$
so $d(L|K)$ is a power of the residue characteristic $p = \mathrm{char}\,Kv$ (and equals $1$ if $p=0$).

A Galois extension $(L|K,v)$ of prime degree $p$ with nontrivial defect (i.e. $d(L|K)=p$) is called an independent defect extension if a certain canonical invariant (the "independent" type of defect, as opposed to "dependent" defect) holds; equivalently, the extension is not generated by an Artin–Schreier–type element whose defect is "linked" to a nontrivial immediate purely wild subextension. Call $(K,v)$ an independent defect field if every Galois defect extension of $(K,v)$ of prime degree has independent defect.

A henselian valued field $(K,v)$ is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if for every finite purely wild extension $(L|K,v)$ the trace ideal/different-type condition characterizing deeply ramified behaviour holds; equivalently, $(K,v)$ shares with deeply ramified and perfectoid fields the property that the module of relative Kähler differentials of every finite extension of its valuation ring vanishes after suitable localization. Every roughly deeply ramified henselian field has the property that all of its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields.

Question. Suppose $(K,v)$ is a henselian valued field such that every algebraic extension $(L|K,v|_L)$ of $(K,v)$ is an independent defect field (that is, every Galois extension of prime degree with nontrivial defect over any algebraic extension of $(K,v)$ has independent defect). Does it follow that $(K,v)$ is a roughly deeply ramified field?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open conjecture in a December 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. One direction (every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field) is known; the converse is stated as an open conjecture, and no resolution appears in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Model theory of tame valued fields and beyond: recent developments and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: we conjecture that a henselian field is a roughly deeply ramified field if and only if all of its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open conjecture/problem; no proof known.

status_evidence.title: The valuation theory of deeply ramified fields and its connection with defect extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Perfectoid and deeply ramified fields only admit extensions with independent defect.
status_evidence.claim: Background showing one direction of the equivalence; the converse remains the open question.
